name: Neo-Thomism
summary: Neo-Thomism is the revival of Thomas Aquinas's philosophy that Leo XIII launched in 1879, and its political side rests on natural law, a common good ordered by reason, and the dignity of the person. Its adherents defend private property and the family against socialism, urge cooperation between capital and labour, and hold that authority comes ultimately from God and is limited by law. In Maritain's version it supports a pluralist democracy with human rights and cooperation between Church and state in separate spheres.
scope: The political thought of the Neo-Thomist revival, built on Leo XIII's Rerum Novarum and the Aquinas political tradition as read by Jacques Maritain (Integral Humanism, Man and the State), the mainstream Catholic Thomism of the mid-20th century. It is a philosophy rather than a party program, so positions the tradition never addressed are answered at low confidence. It does not cover the later papal social encyclicals beyond Rerum Novarum, which were not opened, and it leaves out integralist and traditionalist strands that reject Maritain's democratic pluralism.

keyFigures.name: Jacques Maritain
keyFigures.role: Leading Neo-Thomist political philosopher, author of Integral Humanism and Man and the State.

keyFigures.name: Leo XIII
keyFigures.role: Pope whose Aeterni Patris (1879) launched the Thomist revival and whose Rerum Novarum (1891) set out its social teaching.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from the duty to protect workers and the poor and from Maritain's stress on workers' rights; the sources do not discuss healthcare itself.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Rerum Novarum requires wages sufficient to support a frugal, decent wage-earner, which implies legal support for a living wage, though "substantially" goes beyond the text.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents defend private property and exchange but subordinate markets to justice and the common good, and Maritain refused to merge Christianity with capitalism, so the claim splits them.

public-ownership.rationale: Rerum Novarum insists the state must not absorb private holdings, so wholesale public ownership of major industries is disfavoured, though common-good exceptions are conceivable.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Duties of the rich to give from surplus are taught, but no source speaks to tax rates, so adherents are not committed either way.

unions-good.rationale: Rerum Novarum calls workingmen's associations the most important of all and urges workers to form them, though it prefers religiously grounded ones.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rerum Novarum speaks of the inviolability of private property as grounded in nature, but Aquinas also makes owners distribute their surplus, so it is not absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: State intervention is justified when workers' dignity, health or morals are threatened, which implies regulation of employers; corporations as such are not discussed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Relieving poverty is a duty of justice and charity and public aid is fitting in extreme need; the dependency argument is not a Thomist one.

worker-ownership.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects community of goods and defends private ownership; it wants workers to own property individually rather than own firms collectively.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; common-good reasoning supports security while personalism limits state intrusion, so adherents lean neither way.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from natural-law ethics of temperance and law aimed at the common good; Aquinas says law need not ban every vice, so the position is not firm.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Aquinas holds human law should forbid only graver wrongs, while the common good could justify some limits; adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: Aquinas says even rulers with plenary power are bound by law and that rulers who exceed legal limits become tyrants, so bypassing gridlock by strength is disfavoured.

state-harmful.rationale: The political community exists for the common good and is natural to humans; Aquinas treats the state as necessary, not harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; the common good and a right to self-defence pull in different directions.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; authority to coerce is legitimate for the common good but no funding stance follows from it.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sex outside marriage is wrongful on the Thomist account, so adherents oppose legalising it, though Aquinas held law need not suppress every vice.

decide-locally.rationale: Rerum Novarum limits the state to what is required and holds the family prior to it, the root of subsidiarity, which favours the smaller unit.

rehabilitation.rationale: Aquinas treats punishment as just retribution aiming at the common good, so rehabilitation alone is not the aim, though reform is welcomed.

traditional-family.rationale: Rerum Novarum calls the family a society older than the state with its own rights, and says paternal authority can be neither abolished nor absorbed by the state.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Marriage is understood as ordered to the natural family and to fides and offspring; this follows from core natural-law teaching on sex and marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Natural law protects innocent human life as a basic good and rights are grounded in human nature; this is implied by the core principles rather than quoted in the sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: Rerum Novarum says social peace depends on religion and the Church, and Maritain wants a cooperative Church and state in a new Christian civic order.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Equal dignity is affirmed but remedial programmes are not discussed, and adherents differ on them.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of a shared human nature grounding dignity; gender theory is not addressed by the sources.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's account of civilization and Thomist respect for custom and inherited community, though not directly stated.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred from Aquinas's caution about altering law and respect for established order; not stated in the sources opened.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic thought balances a duty of welcome with a state's prudent care for its common good, so adherents are split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Maritain supports a federation of political societies, provided members keep substantial autonomy.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents differ on trade policy.

nation-first.rationale: Maritain looks to a world federation and people who set aside narrow national interests, so putting national interest above cooperation is disfavoured.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from just-war reasoning that public authority may use force for justice; humanitarian intervention is not discussed.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's federation with autonomous member states; no source addresses borders directly.

limit-growth.rationale: Integral humanism values material welfare alongside the spiritual, and no source calls for limiting growth; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic for the founding texts; adherents are not committed either way.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Maritain holds humans are spiritual as well as material, so technology alone cannot meet human needs; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed and no principle decides it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Aquinas allows subjects to resist and depose tyrants by public action, but Leo XIII rejects class revolution, so adherents are split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Maritain defends democracy and the people's right to govern themselves, which tells against giving experts more say; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects socialism and the abolition of private property as unjust and self-defeating.

socialized-markets.rationale: Worker or public ownership of all business conflicts with Rerum Novarum's defence of individual ownership, though a market element is accepted.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Rerum Novarum grounds property in the family and the father's duty to provide for it, so heavy inheritance taxes cut against that.

basic-income.rationale: Rerum Novarum ties income to work and just wages and aid to need; an unconditional state income is inferred as disfavoured.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state should do no more than needed to protect justice and the common good, so directing investment goes beyond it; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rerum Novarum wants workers able to own property and defends private holdings against socialist absorption.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats wage labour as legitimate and asks for just wages, not its abolition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; a wholesale marketisation of money is not part of the tradition, so inferred as disfavoured.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Rerum Novarum favours workers' associations and cooperation of capital and labour, so corporatist bodies fit, but state-set prices are not stated.

one-party-rule.rationale: Maritain rejects totalitarian regimes and holds that a people has a natural right to govern itself.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Aquinas counts monarchy a legitimate regime within a mixed constitution when bound by law.

democracy-best.rationale: Maritain defends a democratic state grounded in the people's right to govern themselves.

direct-votes.rationale: Aquinas favours a mixed constitution with representative elements rather than rule by direct popular vote; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects class rule by workers and Maritain rejects communism.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; the common good of a complete community is emphasised over fragmentation.

natural-rulers.rationale: Aquinas wants virtuous rulers but Maritain holds that authority rests on the people; adherents differ.

political-violence-never.rationale: Just-war and tyranny-resistance doctrine accepts that force can be justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: War is justified only as a last resort for a just cause, never celebrated for its effect on character.

separate-church-state.rationale: Maritain holds that Church and state cooperate, each in its own sphere, rather than being strictly separated.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Aquinas holds moral norms are knowable by natural reason independently of revelation, so law rests on natural law, not scripture alone.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rerum Novarum makes justice, order and defence the business of the state.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; just-war doctrine fixes the limits of force, not a superiority goal.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Maritain affirms the equal dignity of persons and a pluralistic polity, which tells against an ethnic definition of the nation; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rerum Novarum says conflict between classes is not natural and that capital and labour need each other.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rerum Novarum accepts natural inequalities of condition while demanding justice and relief of poverty.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; justice requires restitution in principle but adherents differ on its application.

civilizational-union.rationale: Maritain looks to a world federation of political societies rather than blocs by religion or civilization; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Thomist ethics aims at the common good and love of neighbour as the supreme principle, not self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Maritain holds rights are inalienable and superior to society though subject to the common good; ranking duties first is not his view.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred from creation doctrine that creatures have goodness of their own; not addressed in the sources.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of human dignity and natural law on the family; coercive limits are not accepted.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Integral humanism seeks to renew civilization, not repudiate it; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Institutions embodying the common good are not to be sacrificed for speed; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: The doctrine of a shared human nature grounding dignity tells against redesigning it; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Law is an ordinance of reason by responsible rulers for the common good, which implies human accountability; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A modern technical question that Thomist sources never touch, and no principle of natural law settles it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Maritain proposed a new Christendom, not a return to the medieval one, and aims at renewal.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Moral principles from natural law bind regardless of results, so judging by outcomes alone is disfavoured.

direct-action.rationale: Maritain advocates working through a democratic state and civic fraternities; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Moral norms bind action in itself, so means must be good, though the statement is framed in anarchist terms; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Integral humanism seeks fulfilment of human nature in civilization and the political community, which is natural to humans.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rerum Novarum accepts differences of function and class; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Aquinas obliges owners to distribute surplus to the needy but retains property and desert, so need is not the sole rule.

production-for-use.rationale: Maritain rejects profit-centred capitalism but not profit as such; adherents differ.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rerum Novarum holds capital and labour cooperate and that property is legitimate, not exploitation by nature, though cheating workers of wages is a grave wrong.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Maritain rejects communism and all dehumanizing regimes.

collective-farming.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends private ownership of land that a person has worked.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of Marxist theory.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state and its law are natural and serve the common good, so taxation is legitimate in principle.

harm-principle.rationale: Aquinas holds law aims at the common good and virtue, though it forbids only the graver vices, so more than harm to others may be restricted.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rerum Novarum gives the family rights prior to the state and endorses associations, so rights are not only individual.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from just-war doctrine and duties to the common good; not discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Maritain values democratic participation as a right of the people, so exit cannot replace the vote; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The state serves the common good, not customers; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Rerum Novarum links just wages and conditions to workers' ability to live decently, which fits material means for freedom; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: A sociological claim about elites that the Thomist sources never make, so no stand follows from them.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Shared human nature and equal dignity are central; the empirical claim is not discussed.

organic-representation.rationale: Rerum Novarum's emphasis on families and associations as natural bodies inclines toward representation through them; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Rerum Novarum says the state must not do more than required, and Maritain's personalism denies that persons are subordinated to the state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Maritain rejects fascism and radical nationalist regeneration; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Just war requires a just cause, which conquest lacks; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Aquinas bases rule on law for the common good and not on personal fealty; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats workers as persons not bondsmen, and a just contract requires freedom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Thomists hold moral truths are knowable by natural reason and not a function of power.

universal-morality.rationale: Aquinas holds moral norms are knowable by natural reason, and Maritain affirms natural law across humanity.

single-common-good.rationale: Political community exists for the common good which law must aim at, though Maritain admits a plural polity.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship and return rights for diasporas lie outside the tradition's texts, and its principles give no clear direction.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language policy is not discussed in Rerum Novarum or Maritain, and no Thomist principle decides it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends the employer's property and authority while requiring justice and respect; democratic voting is not endorsed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from the family's prior rights over education and subsidiarity.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is outside the sources, which give principles of justice but not budget rules.

economic-freedom.rationale: Property is a natural right but Maritain rejects equating Christianity with capitalism; adherents differ.

rule-by-example.rationale: Aquinas holds law needs coercive force in the actual world, so moral example alone is not enough.

national-self-determination.rationale: Maritain holds that peoples have a natural right to govern themselves; its extension to nations is inferred.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; just-war doctrine asks for legitimate authority but adherents differ on the UN.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Neo-scholasticism holds that grace perfects nature and that faith and reason cooperate; reason alone is not the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Universal human dignity and the duty to the poor wherever they live tell against excluding immigrants; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; Rerum Novarum values work but also relief of the needy.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rerum Novarum states that capital cannot do without labour nor labour without capital and calls for cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Neo-scholasticism is a revival of an inherited tradition and prizes institutions that preserve it.

dominated-front.rationale: Maritain favours cooperative federation, not blocs against the West; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; Rerum Novarum treats classes as cooperating.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Rerum Novarum assigns the father authority in the family but modern adherents differ on law and public roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Aquinas judged usury contrary to just equality, but modern Thomists accept interest; adherents are split.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Maritain's doctrine of equal natural rights and personal dignity excludes racial classification.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rerum Novarum says the state protects justice and rights for all, not a class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for these sources, and no principle of the tradition decides it.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Maritain's pluralist polity respects differences; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in the documented doctrine; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed by Aquinas or Maritain, who care about the form of regime rather than the voting formula.

national-mission.rationale: Maritain favours pluralism and federation; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats the family order as natural; the structural-patriarchy claim is inferred as rejected.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not addressed beyond Aquinas's account of tyranny.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inalienable personal rights and dignity forbid state compulsion over procreation.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Law binds rulers and the state serves justice; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rerum Novarum allows intervention when workers' dignity, family life, morals or health are threatened.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equal dignity and the natural right to marry exclude race-based discouragement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Maritain holds persons have inalienable natural rights from a shared human nature.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist question on which Thomists, who reject socialism, have no stake.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: A contemporary debate that these sources do not address, and adherents have no shared view.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; family autonomy and uniform law pull in different directions.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Maritain stresses freedom of conscience, so legal limits on conversion are disfavoured, but the tradition has some support for them.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Aquinas allows use of animals for human purposes; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Rerum Novarum holds religion essential to society and gives parents prior rights over schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Maritain rejects communism and totalising states; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Maritain holds authority derives from the people with God as ultimate source.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade aims are not addressed, and Thomism offers no ruling on them.

population-transfer.rationale: Inalienable personal rights exclude forcing minorities out.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Aquinas accepts force in just war and punishment, so initiation is not always wrong.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rerum Novarum emphasises cooperation between classes and charity over struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Law that aims at the common good may restrain threats to the community; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Aquinas's account of tyranny matches some of it but the idea is not found in the sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Aquinas holds the best constitution mixes monarchy, aristocracy and democracy, with power limited by law.

vanguard-party.rationale: Maritain rejects communism and holds the people have a right to self-government.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rerum Novarum says workers' interests deserve special state protection since they have fewer resources.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred from Rerum Novarum's wish for workers to become owners.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Rerum Novarum says strikes disrupt public peace and the law should remove their causes, so adherents differ on restricting them.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Rerum Novarum locates poverty in injustice and wages, not demography; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Maritain defends a pluralist polity; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Aquinas wants rulers chosen for their fitness, not by chance; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Natural rights are inalienable and superior to society, which tells against suspending them; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The just price tradition allows limits but the sources opened do not cover it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Maritain rejects totalitarian regimes and defends freedom of conscience.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not covered in the sources, and the tradition leaves them to prudence.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; rulers are to be worthy and need not be paid like workers; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Aquinas holds conscience binds even when mistaken, which tells against binding party discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Maritain supports a federation of political societies with substantial autonomy for members.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Who commands the army is a constitutional detail Aquinas and Maritain do not settle beyond limits of law.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Catholic neo-scholasticism worked in a hierarchical, episcopally governed Church; the national-church framing is inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Aquinas holds that church leaders have no jurisdiction over secular matters.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Aquinas allows just war by legitimate authority, so a general call for defeat is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Aquinas lets law restrain graver vices, while Maritain stresses freedom of conscience; adherents are split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term rules are not addressed; Aquinas's concern is that rulers stay bound by law, not how long they serve.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall mechanisms are not discussed in the sources opened, and the tradition leaves them to prudence.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not covered, and just-war teaching does not decide for or against permanent alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends private ownership, including of land, and does not require equal home ownership by law.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; defence is the state's task; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources make no comparison between rural and urban life, and Thomism has no doctrine on it.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of divided states is not addressed, and no Thomist principle decides it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition values learning; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Moral truths hold across cultures and are known by reason, so cultures can be judged by that standard.

death-penalty.rationale: Aquinas holds public authority may intend death as punishment, but modern adherents are split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Parents' prior rights over children's formation tell against state-set sex education; the gender-equality part is inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Neo-scholasticism holds that faith and reason cooperate and philosophy and science have their own domain; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Aquinas holds law may restrain the graver vices for the common good; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The basis of citizenship is not discussed by the sources, so no position follows.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Maritain stresses freedom of conscience and Aquinas holds conscience binds even when mistaken.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Customary order and virtue are valued; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief for poor countries is outside the sources, though duties of aid pull one way and just contracts the other.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A question from anti-colonial thought that the sources never address.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Procedures for writing constitutions are not discussed, and the tradition leaves them to prudence.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rights are inalienable and superior to society, so they cannot be traded for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aquinas makes relieving poverty a duty of justice and charity and obliges owners to distribute their surplus.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear strategy is anachronistic for the sources, and just-war reasoning does not decide it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The mode of choosing a head of state is not settled beyond Aquinas's view that election is probably better than heredity for a monarch.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed in the sources, so no stand follows.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial compromise is not addressed, and the tradition gives no rule on it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Aquinas justifies private property by its benefits and requires owners to distribute their surplus.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist dispute on which Thomists take no side.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; prudence is a virtue but no rule follows.

collective-defense.rationale: Just-war doctrine allows defence of others by legitimate authority; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The status of annexed territory is not covered, though just-war ideas of just cause bear on it only loosely.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Maritain holds Church and state cooperate in separate spheres, and Aquinas treats them as distinct complete communities.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a head of state above party is not addressed in the sources opened.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The sources do not address secession by force, and the common-good emphasis cuts both ways.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with autonomy and federation.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Authority derives from God but Aquinas holds absolute political authority is contrary to his teaching and rulers are bound by law.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not discussed, and Rerum Novarum gives no preference between flat and graduated rates.

character-from-environment.rationale: Thomism holds a shared human nature and free will; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Aquinas holds that even rulers with plenary power are bound by law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a central goal for a tradition focused on the spiritual end of persons; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Aquinas holds that the best government is a mixed constitution combining monarchy, aristocracy and democracy.

leader-cult.rationale: Maritain rejects fascism and totalitarianism, and persons cannot be subordinated to the state.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are not addressed in the sources opened, and no clear Thomist principle decides it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question on which Thomists have no stake.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends the inviolability of private property, including land.

refugee-return.rationale: The right of refugees' descendants to return is not addressed by the sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Just war needs a just cause; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Aquinas allowed compulsion of baptized believers but Maritain stresses freedom of conscience, so modern adherents oppose it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; no Thomist basis for legal dress codes; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not discussed, though Maritain's federation idea is compatible with it, so no clear stand follows.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Maritain's federation is among political societies, not kin peoples; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Whether persecuted minorities should emigrate or fight for rights is not addressed in these sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Maritain's integral humanism holds human beings are spiritual as well as material, and he rejects Marxism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The state protects justice in economic life; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescue policy is outside the sources, and no principle of justice they give decides it.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Maritain holds natural law and rights are superior to society and positive law contradicting them is not law.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from complementarity of family roles; not addressed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Maritain looks to world federation; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Protecting workers' dignity is a duty of justice; extension to trade agreements is inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equal dignity of persons and the common good limit owners' freedom; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Law serves the common good of the whole community, which a single dissenter cannot block.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The tradition permits use of animals for human ends, with restraint on cruelty; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Rerum Novarum tells the wealthy to treat workers as persons and to give from surplus to the needy, and Aquinas says the same of surplus.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The political community is natural and serves the common good, so withdrawal is not the best life; inferred.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Marxist critique of mass culture that the Thomist sources never take up.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The cultural hegemony thesis is a Marxist idea outside these sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is outside the Thomist sources and adherents have no shared position on it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equal dignity tells against reserving offices by birth; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: A Marxist question on which Thomists have no stake.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Duties of aid from surplus tell against refusing aid; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Just war requires just cause and last resort; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal political rights for all citizens is the democratic norm for Maritain; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical question not addressed; the tradition's equal-dignity stance suggests rejection; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is a contemporary controversy not addressed in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Public programme priorities by sex are not addressed, and no Thomist principle decides it.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Service provision by sex of victim is not addressed, and the tradition gives no ruling.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Authority rests on law and the common good, not on military guardianship; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; family life is valued but pay is not discussed.

filial-duty.rationale: The Decalogue norms, including honouring parents, are knowable by reason and bind.

office-by-exam.rationale: Recruitment by examination is not discussed; Aquinas wants fit rulers but names no method.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Industrial and investment policy is not addressed in the sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Rerum Novarum treats the family as a natural society and Catholic teaching holds marriage indissoluble; inferred from core principles.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Aquinas holds conscience binds, and Maritain's representative democracy is not mandate-bound; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is outside the sources opened, which give no stand on funded or pay-as-you-go schemes.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends private ownership of land that a person has worked.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not discussed, though law-bound rule makes it consistent; the sources give no stand.

single-official-language.rationale: Maritain's pluralist polity respects difference; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign ownership of land is not addressed, and no Thomist principle decides it.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Justice concerns acts and intentions toward persons; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Integral humanism holds that human beings have a spiritual nature that material pursuits alone do not satisfy.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Just-war doctrine requires legitimate authority and last resort; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Force needs just cause and legitimate authority; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Rerum Novarum worries about the strong overpowering workers; inferred for lobbying.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The family is the foundation of society and the state may aid it; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on purchases are not addressed in the sources.

non-intervention.rationale: Just-war doctrine allows force for justice by legitimate authority; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed; Rerum Novarum is open as to type.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy accusation against a group contradicts equal dignity and Maritain's pluralism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage and the family are natural institutions with their own standing that the state recognises.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information is not discussed in the sources.

local-production.rationale: Localism in trade is not addressed, though subsidiarity points toward it only loosely.

informal-organisation.rationale: The tradition favours established associations and unions; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Maritain favours federation and natural law above positive law; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Maritain's polity is pluralistic and recognises differences of religious conscience.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Maritain looks to federation of autonomous societies; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Common good and solidarity tell against regional hoarding; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends private ownership of what a person earns, which covers personal belongings, while rejecting common ownership of everything.

defeat-communism.rationale: Maritain rejects communism but favoured cooperation among believers and others; adherents differ on method.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Subsidiarity and associations favour plural providers; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Maritain rejects secular humanisms and holds that persons have a spiritual nature and destiny.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not addressed; Maritain was uninterested in combining Christianity with capitalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The tradition does not treat the economy as source of women's position; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Rerum Novarum holds that the family's authority can be neither abolished nor absorbed by the state.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not addressed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects community of goods.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from equal dignity and pluralism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Maritain's personalism is a middle path between individualism and socialism, and he is not interested in combining Christianity with capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or religious claims to land are not addressed, and adherents have no common view.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Maritain affirmed human dignity against totalitarian atrocity; denial is not a position of the tradition.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Same-sex relations are held wrong but Aquinas says law forbids only graver vices and Maritain stresses conscience; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Maritain rejects totalitarian rule and holds in democracy dissenting minorities play an important role.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Aquinas allowed secular punishment of public heresy but Maritain's pluralist polity does not.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Rulers must govern for the common good of the community, not for the benefit of another country.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Resistance is for tyranny and law-breaking rulers, not religious difference; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Subsidiarity and civic fraternities favour participation but no source states it.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A critical-theory claim that the tradition does not share; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of a shared human nature.

assisted-dying.rationale: Natural law protects innocent life and suicide and killing are wrong; this follows from core principles.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Maritain sought a third way beyond both but adherents differ.

alienated-labor.rationale: Rerum Novarum condemns treating workers as tools but not in Marxist terms.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Maritain's pluralism and cooperation of believers tell against it; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Maritain grounds democracy in God as ultimate source of authority and Aquinas derives political authority from divine authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Maritain stresses freedom of conscience; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment-law procedure is not addressed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Rerum Novarum accepts private property and markets within justice and state protection of workers; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Just-war doctrine accepts that public authority may use force in defence.

rich-first.rationale: Development sequencing is not addressed, and the tradition's concern for the poor does not decide it.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Alliance neutrality is not addressed, and just-war doctrine leaves it to prudence.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Aquinas accepts monarchy but thinks election better; adherents differ.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Aquinas condemned usury but the modern tradition accepts interest; adherents differ.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Conditions on international loans are outside the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: Maritain holds the people have the right to govern themselves; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim not shared; inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept about commodity relations that the Thomist sources never discuss.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A Marxist claim; the tradition defends freedoms of conscience and assembly; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Aquinas defines law as an ordinance of reason for the common good promulgated by those responsible for the community.

racial-franchise.rationale: Equal natural rights and the people's right to self-government exclude racial limits.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is anachronistic for the sources and no principle decides it.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data practice is anachronistic for the sources, and none of them takes a stand.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Maritain recognises differences of religious conscience; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Equal dignity and pluralism exclude targeting a religious minority.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Randomly selected deliberative bodies are not addressed; the tradition's mixed constitution does not decide it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Neo-scholasticism is a revival of an authoritative inherited doctrine; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Rerum Novarum wants wide ownership and warns against exploitation of workers by the strong; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the Thomist account of sexual ethics.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Maritain rejects secular humanisms and communism and recognises God's sovereignty.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Law needs coercive force in the actual world, and public authority may punish.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Rerum Novarum stresses charity and relief organisations with public aid in extreme need; subsidiarity inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Limits on terms are not addressed, and the tradition leaves it to prudence.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is anachronistic and not covered by the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction-risk policy is not addressed, and no Thomist principle ranks it.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Catholic neo-scholasticism upholds the all-male priesthood; inferred from core doctrine.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Rerum Novarum assigns the father authority but modern adherents differ.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voting rights of foreign residents are not addressed in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Housing price policy is not addressed in the sources opened, and the just-price idea does not clearly decide it.

abolish-ip.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends ownership of the fruits of labour; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled national youth movements belong to the totalitarian regimes Maritain rejects; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Basing of nuclear weapons is anachronistic for the sources, and none gives a stand.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is not addressed, and just-war doctrine leaves it to prudence.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Justice for atrocities fits the tradition; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Rerum Novarum values wages for labour but defends property and its returns.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Aquinas allows lethal defence under just-war and punishment reasoning; self-defence follows by double effect.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: A myth-of-origin claim not addressed by the Thomist sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from shared human nature and natural law.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring national dead as saints is not part of the tradition; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora-homeland relations are not addressed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred; the tradition treats scripture as authoritative.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Equal dignity tells against ethnic economic limits; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A Marxist question on which Thomists have no stake.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Which services should be public is not specified in the sources, and subsidiarity does not settle it.

second-chamber.rationale: A mixed constitution suggests multiple bodies; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects community of goods.

family-wage.rationale: Rerum Novarum requires wages sufficient to support a frugal wage-earner.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is an anachronistic question the sources do not address.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Research funding priorities are not addressed in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Maritain holds persons cannot be fully subordinated to the social order and the state serves the person.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Integral humanism treats the human being as both material and spiritual.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Subsidiarity favours stable lower-level authority; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology is not addressed by the sources and no principle decides it.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban form is not addressed in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Common good and equal dignity tell against racial organising; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: The legitimacy of racial pride is not addressed in the sources, and adherents differ.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Aquinas lets war punish injustice as well as defend, but adherents differ today.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's plural polity and political societies.

communal-electorates.rationale: Maritain's civic fraternities are pluralist but not sectarian electorates; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: A conspiratorial claim not part of the doctrine; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Higher-education funding is not addressed in the sources.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental tax design is not addressed in the sources opened.

future-generations.rationale: The common good extends over time; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from complementarity of roles in the Catholic tradition.

arms-reduction.rationale: Maritain's federation aims at peace; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secrecy in treaties is not addressed in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital movement policy is not addressed in the sources.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Public authority holds the right to use force; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Aquinas allows just war by legitimate authority, though conscience binds against unjust orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Rerum Novarum favours workers' associations that bargain over wages and conditions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Wage top-ups are not addressed, though Rerum Novarum's living wage idea does not specify the mechanism.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Legal limits on borrowing are not addressed in the sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The state is natural and needed for the common good.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural capital accounting is anachronistic and outside the sources.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loan policy is outside the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: A theory of regional exploitation that the sources do not take up.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Maritain grounds natural law and rights in human nature, which Neo-Thomism holds is shared and not to be redesigned.

public-service-media.rationale: Public broadcasting is not addressed in the sources.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Maritain accepted religious pluralism in the polity without holding that all religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: The just-price tradition is relevant but no source opened addresses it.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear disarmament policy is anachronistic for the sources, and just-war reasoning does not settle it.

workers-own-party.rationale: Not addressed; Rerum Novarum rejects class politics but accepts workers' associations.

ban-fgm.rationale: Bodily integrity and natural dignity; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal natural rights of persons; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic naming dispute that the sources do not address.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The legal mechanism for pollution harm is not addressed in the sources.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary chiefs in national lawmaking are not addressed in the sources.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Trade-offs between environment and liberty are not addressed in the sources.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sentencing discretion is not addressed in the sources opened.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language requirements for immigrants are not addressed in the sources.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Rerum Novarum favours unions but does not address compulsion.

voter-id.rationale: Voter identification rules are not addressed in the sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Maritain recognises religious pluralism but Catholic doctrine claims a special status; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Maritain grounds democracy in natural law and Christian inspiration, not merely procedure.

premarital-sex.rationale: Sex outside marriage is wrongful on the Thomist account of marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Freedom of conscience limits such measures; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from preference for work-based wages and charity.

women-suffrage.rationale: Maritain's democratic doctrine rests on the people's right to govern themselves; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Rerum Novarum and Catholic teaching treat family and religion as protecting dignity.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; adherents accept human unity but differ on the science.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Institutional machinery for gender equality is not addressed in the sources.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Aquinas holds resources are common by nature but ownership is justified by use, so adherents are split.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Maritain supports federation and universal rights; inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Thomism reads scripture by multiple senses rather than only literally; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Gender guarantees in indigenous self-government are not addressed in the sources.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects socialist ownership; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Mixed constitution allows varied selection; not addressed.

national-church-status.rationale: Adherents differ between confessional states and Maritain's pluralist polity.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Territorial autonomy for minorities is not addressed beyond Maritain's general pluralism and subsidiarity.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Plebiscites for disputed territory are not addressed in the sources.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The inheritance of colonial borders is not addressed in the sources.

equal-conscription.rationale: Conscription of women is not addressed in the sources.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Aquinas allows death only by public authority in punishment after judgement.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Aquinas holds natural resources are common by nature yet private property justified, so adherents are split.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Consumption tax levels are not addressed in the sources.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Targeting versus universality in social spending is not addressed in the sources opened.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Maritain rejects totalitarian leader rule and values civic fraternities.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Justice in economic life favours equal treatment; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Maritain wanted a Christian-inspired civic order, and the Catholic tradition has had confessional parties; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The blend of technology and ancestral values is not addressed in the sources.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Marriage is held indissoluble, so unilateral divorce is disfavoured; inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: National control over natural resources is not addressed beyond Aquinas's note that resources are common by nature.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Maritain holds that positive law contradicting natural law is not really law, following Aquinas.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Rerum Novarum defends rightful acquisition and accepts natural inequality, but Thomist teaching ties property to the common good and duties of charity, so a pure process test is not endorsed; inferred, not discussed directly.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is wary of usury and speculation but the sources say nothing on a levy on currency trades.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's insistence on the equal dignity of every person and his support for universal human rights, which implies racism remains a real wrong; modern racial disparities are not discussed.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Rerum Novarum's view of labour as dignified and tied to family support, which suggests keeping people in work rather than minimising it; automation is not discussed.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's support for international order and human rights institutions, though Thomism has no stated view on balance among great powers.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Rerum Novarum praises labour as the source of property, but Thomist just-price thinking looks to need and the common estimate, not labour alone; adherents are not committed either way.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: the tradition values love of country as a natural duty and urges a politics that protects workers, though Maritain rejects nationalism.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: the question is about priorities within the left, which Neo-Thomists, who reject socialism, never addressed; personalism values both material welfare and spiritual dignity.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Rerum Novarum rejects socialism as unjust to property and Maritain rejects communism and party dictatorship, so a party-led socialist economy is opposed.

missingStatements.text: An unjust law is not truly law and does not bind in conscience.
missingStatements.rationale: Maritain holds that positive law contradicting natural law is not really law, following Aquinas.

missingStatements.text: Church and state should cooperate, each in its own sphere, rather than being separated or merged.
missingStatements.rationale: Maritain makes the state responsible for temporal matters and the Church for spiritual ones in cooperation, and Aquinas treats them as distinct complete communities.
missingStatements.declined: Low-inclusion position (+1) between separation and merger; separate-church-state and more-religion-public already place the ideology.

missingStatements.text: Larger bodies such as the state should help families and associations but never absorb or replace them.
missingStatements.rationale: Rerum Novarum says paternal authority can be neither abolished nor absorbed by the state and that law must not go further than required.

notes: Pre-conciliar manualist Thomists would answer more strictly on religious establishment, blasphemy and apostasy than the Maritain mainstream used here. Modern Catholic teaching on the death penalty has shifted, hence low confidence.
